title: Qodo Pricing: Every Plan, Price and Limit (2026)
summary: Qodo pricing includes free and paid plans with varying limits on code reviews and AI features.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


### Is Qodo free for open-source projects?


Qodo has a free individual tier, and its open-source PR-Agent project can be run on your own infrastructure. We haven't confirmed a separate free arrangement for open-source maintainers on the hosted product.


If you maintain a public repository, ask Qodo before assuming one exists. Otherwise you may find out when the free tier's usage limit runs out mid-month and the next plan is the one you're offered.


### Does Qodo charge per pull request or per seat?


Qodo sells its paid plans by credit pack rather than per seat, but the pack price is only half the bill, because overage is billed on top of it. However few people you have, open many pull requests and a plan's cap can arrive before the month ends.


Count your pull requests per month and compare that number to the limit on each plan, not just the price per person.


If you cancel or downgrade mid-month, we haven't confirmed Qodo's exact terms, so read them before you commit.


Two questions decide the cost: does a downgrade take effect immediately or at the end of the billing period, and does unused usage carry over? If you cancel and the answer is "no refund, no carry-over," you've paid for days you can't use.


Don't budget on an annual discount, because we haven't confirmed one for Qodo.


If you plan to pay yearly, get the discount in writing first. Paying a year up front for a plan whose usage cap you outgrow in month three locks in the wrong tier.


### Is the Qodo IDE plugin priced separately from code review?


We haven't confirmed whether Qodo prices its IDE plugin and its code review as separate line items, or counts both against one shared usage limit. The difference matters.


If both draw on one pool, a developer who leans on the plugin all week leaves less for review on Friday. Ask which activities count toward the same limit before you size a plan.
